The Anambra State Commissioner of Police, Nnanna Ama, has called for stronger police-citizen relations through mutual trust, respect for human rights, effective communication and community participation. Ama said public confidence and community involvement were indispensable to sustainable security. He stated this on Friday during a one-day summit themed ‘You and the Police’, held at the Faculty of Social Sciences, Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Awka, Anambra State. The summit provided a platform for engagement between the police and members of the academic community, particularly students, on their respective roles in maintaining security. Speaking at the event, the commissioner emphasised that effective policing went beyond law enforcement and the maintenance of public order. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources He said, “Public trust, community participation, timely intelligence sharing, accountability and respect for the rights and dignity of citizens remain fundamental pillars of effective and sustainable security. Jigawa police boss begs traditional institutions to address security concerns Police arrest 45 during criminal hideout raids in Anambra Enugu CP pledges to sanction erring officers, reward best performers “We encourage students and academics to see the Police as partners in progress and not merely as an institution of law enforcement. “They should embrace constructive engagement, responsible citizenship, lawful conduct and timely sharing of credible information to address security challenges.” Those in attendance included the Commandant of the Anambra State Correctional Centre, representatives of the Department of State Services, Federal Road Safety Corps and National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, as well as the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Academic), Prof. Alex Akadi, who represented the university’s Vice-Chancellor. Other academics and relevant stakeholders also attended the summit. Highlights of the event included goodwill messages from sister security agencies and other stakeholders, as well as the presentation of Awards of Excellence to the commissioner and other recipients in recognition of their contributions.
